newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court upholds Community goods trading statistics regime.
newsitem.headline: Court upholds Community goods trading statistics regime.

text.p: The European Court of Justice found on Wednesday that the Community statistical system known as Intrastat, which measures the amount of goods traded between member states, is justified and valid.
Intrastat was challenged by defendants in a criminal trial in Luxembourg as a constraint against trade. The defendants were found guilty of not declaring traded goods to the appropriate authorities.

The court recognized that reporting requirements might have restrictive effects on trade, but said they were "essential in order to obtain reasonably complete and accurate information on movements of goods within the Community.
"The aim pursued by the regulation, namely to promote completion of the internal market by establishing statistics on the trading of goods between member states, appears justified," the court said.
The court noted that Community institutions have offered, free of charge, modern data-processing tools such as the IDEP/CN8 data capture software.
"Free movement of goods - Articles 30 and 34 of the EC Treaty"

Examination of Council regulation (EEC) No 3330/91 on the statistics relating to the trading of goods between member states has not disclosed any factor of such a kind as to cast doubt on its validity.
